subject: Other Subjects (Ethics, Biostatistics, Research Methodology & Medical Jurisprudence Overlap)

subtopics: Definition and scope of medical ethics
Bioethics vs medical ethics vs clinical ethics
Four principles of biomedical ethics (Beauchamp & Childress) — autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice
Principle of autonomy — respect for patient's decision-making, capacity assessment
Principle of beneficence — duty to act in patient's best interest, paternalism vs shared decision-making
Principle of non-maleficence — "primum non nocere," balancing harm and benefit
Principle of justice — distributive justice, resource allocation, triage ethics
Deontological ethics (Kantian) — duty-based approach in medicine
Consequentialism/utilitarianism — outcome-based ethical reasoning
Virtue ethics — character of the physician
Hippocratic Oath — historical significance, modern relevance
Declaration of Geneva (Physician's Pledge) — WMA, modern Hippocratic Oath
Declaration of Helsinki — ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects
Nuremberg Code — origin, ten principles, historical context
Belmont Report — respect for persons, beneficence, justice in research
International ethical guidelines — WMA declarations (Tokyo, Lisbon, Malta, Ottawa)
Indian Medical Council (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations, 2002
National Medical Commission (NMC) — role in ethics regulation, replacement of MCI
Ethical committees — Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC), composition, functions, ICMR guidelines
Informed consent — definition, elements (disclosure, understanding, voluntariness, capacity, authorization)
Types of consent — implied, expressed (oral, written), blanket consent
Capacity/competence to consent — assessment, fluctuating capacity
Consent in minors — age of consent, parental/guardian consent, mature minor doctrine, Gillick competence
Consent in mentally ill patients — Mental Healthcare Act 2017, advance directives, nominated representative
Consent in unconscious/emergency patients — doctrine of necessity, implied consent in emergencies
Therapeutic privilege — withholding information, ethical justification, limitations
Right to refuse treatment — competent adults, Jehovah's Witnesses, hunger strikes
Consent for surgical procedures — specific vs general consent, scope of consent
Consent in research — additional requirements, IRB/IEC approval, vulnerable populations
Consent for HIV testing — pre-test and post-test counseling, confidentiality
Consent in organ donation — living donor, cadaveric donor, THOA 1994
Proxy consent / surrogate decision-making — hierarchy of surrogates
Withdrawal of consent — patient's right to withdraw at any time
Documentation of consent — legal requirements, best practices
Duty of confidentiality — ethical and legal basis
Doctor-patient privilege — scope, limitations
Exceptions to confidentiality — statutory reporting (notifiable diseases, gunshot wounds, child abuse), court orders, public interest
Confidentiality in HIV/AIDS — disclosure to spouse/partner, ethical dilemma
Confidentiality of medical records — storage, access, electronic health records
Breach of confidentiality — legal consequences, disciplinary action
Confidentiality in genetic information — implications for family members
Confidentiality in adolescent healthcare — reproductive health, substance abuse
Information Technology Act 2000 and health data — digital privacy
Telemedicine and confidentiality — Telemedicine Practice Guidelines 2020
Euthanasia — definition, types (active, passive, voluntary, involuntary, non-voluntary)
Legal status of euthanasia — India (Aruna Shanbaug case, Common Cause vs Union of India 2018), international comparison
Passive euthanasia in India — Supreme Court guidelines, living will/advance directive
Advance directives — legal validity in India, format, execution, safeguards
Physician-assisted suicide — definition, ethical arguments, legal status
Withdrawal and withholding of life-sustaining treatment — ethical framework, medical futility
Medical futility — definition, quantitative vs qualitative, who decides
Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR) — ethical basis, documentation, communication
Palliative care ethics — goals, symptom management, principle of double effect
Principle of double effect — conditions for ethical justification, application in pain management
Brain death — ethical implications, organ donation, family communication
Organ donation ethics — consent models (opt-in vs opt-out), living donor ethics, commercialization
Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act (THOA) 1994 (amended 2011) — provisions, authorization committee
Terminal sedation — ethical considerations
Quality of life vs sanctity of life — ethical debate
Doctor-patient relationship — models (paternalistic, informative, interpretive, deliberative)
Shared decision-making — principles, tools, patient-centered care
Professional boundaries — dual relationships, gifts, social media
Conflict of interest — disclosure, management, pharmaceutical industry interactions
Medical advertising and self-promotion — NMC regulations, ethical advertising
Second opinion — patient's right, physician's duty
Referral ethics — appropriate referral, fee-splitting (dichotomy), kickbacks
Whistle-blowing in medicine — duty to report, protection of whistleblowers
Impaired physician — substance abuse, mental health, fitness to practice
Professional misconduct — definition, examples, disciplinary proceedings by NMC/State Medical Councils
Duties of a physician — to patients, to colleagues, to society, to self
Communication skills — breaking bad news (SPIKES protocol), truth-telling, empathy
Cultural competence — respecting diverse beliefs, religious considerations in treatment
Social media ethics — patient privacy, professional image, online consultations
Telemedicine ethics — Telemedicine Practice Guidelines 2020, limitations, prescribing
Indian Medical Council Act 1956 — establishment of MCI, functions (now replaced by NMC)
National Medical Commission Act 2019 — structure, functions, NEXT exam, autonomous boards
Consumer Protection Act 2019 (CPA) — applicability to medical profession, deficiency in service, medical negligence
Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act 2010 — registration, standards
Mental Healthcare Act 2017 — rights of mentally ill, advance directives, decriminalization of suicide attempt
Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016 — reasonable accommodation, non-discrimination
Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act 1994 — prohibition of sex determination, penalties
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act 1971 (amended 2021) — indications, gestational limits (20 weeks, 24 weeks for special categories), opinion requirements, confidentiality
Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 — drug regulation, schedule H, H1, X drugs
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act 1985 — controlled substances, prescribing regulations
Epidemic Diseases Act 1897 — powers during epidemics, COVID-19 amendments
Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016 — categories, color coding, treatment, disposal
Human Organ Transplantation Act (THOA) 1994 — brain death certification, authorization committee, penalties for organ trade
Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) Regulation Act 2021 and Surrogacy Regulation Act 2021
Right to health — Article 21, Parmanand Katara case, duty to treat in emergencies
Definition and scope of biostatistics
Types of data — qualitative (nominal, ordinal), quantitative (discrete, continuous), interval, ratio scales
Measures of central tendency — mean (arithmetic, geometric, harmonic), median, mode
Properties of mean, median, mode — when to use each, effect of skewness
Measures of dispersion — range, interquartile range, variance, standard deviation, coefficient of variation
Standard deviation vs standard error — distinction, calculation, interpretation
Normal (Gaussian) distribution — properties, 68-95-99.7 rule, Z-scores
Skewness and kurtosis — positive skew, negative skew, leptokurtic, platykurtic
Non-normal distributions — binomial, Poisson, log-normal
Frequency distribution — tables, histograms, frequency polygons, ogive curves
Data presentation — tables, bar charts, pie charts, line graphs, box-and-whisker plots, scatter plots
Percentiles, quartiles, deciles — calculation, interpretation
Correlation — Pearson's correlation coefficient (r), Spearman's rank correlation, interpretation, correlation vs causation
Regression — simple linear regression, regression equation, coefficient of determination (r²)
Coefficient of variation — comparing variability between different datasets

topics.topic: Biostatistics — Inferential Statistics & Hypothesis Testing (~20 questions)
subtopics: Population vs sample — parameters vs statistics
Sampling methods — simple random, systematic, stratified, cluster, multistage, convenience, snowball, purposive
Sampling error vs non-sampling error (bias)
Sample size determination — factors affecting, formula for proportions and means, power analysis
Probability — basic concepts, addition and multiplication rules, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem
Confidence intervals — 95% CI, 99% CI, interpretation, relationship to hypothesis testing
Hypothesis testing — null hypothesis (H₀), alternative hypothesis (H₁), one-tailed vs two-tailed tests
Type I error (α) — false positive, significance level (p < 0.05)
Type II error (β) — false negative, power of a test (1 − β)
p-value — definition, interpretation, limitations, p-value vs clinical significance
Student's t-test — paired, unpaired (independent), assumptions, when to use
Chi-square test (χ²) — test of association, goodness of fit, Yates' correction, assumptions
Fisher's exact test — when to use (small sample sizes, expected frequency < 5)
ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) — one-way, two-way, post-hoc tests (Tukey, Bonferroni)
Non-parametric tests — Mann-Whitney U test, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Kruskal-Wallis test, Friedman test
When to use parametric vs non-parametric tests — assumptions, decision flowchart
Multiple comparisons — Bonferroni correction, false discovery rate
Odds ratio (OR) — calculation, interpretation, use in case-control studies
Relative risk (RR) — calculation, interpretation, use in cohort studies
Absolute risk reduction (ARR), relative risk reduction (RRR), number needed to treat (NNT), number needed to harm (NNH)
Sensitivity — definition, calculation, true positive rate, SnNOut (high sensitivity rules out)
Specificity — definition, calculation, true negative rate, SpPIn (high specificity rules in)
Positive predictive value (PPV) — definition, calculation, effect of prevalence
Negative predictive value (NPV) — definition, calculation, effect of prevalence
Prevalence and its effect on PPV and NPV
2×2 contingency table — construction, calculation of sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV
False positive rate and false negative rate
Accuracy — overall proportion of correct results
Likelihood ratios — positive LR (LR+), negative LR (LR−), interpretation, Fagan nomogram
Pre-test and post-test probability — Bayesian approach
ROC curve (Receiver Operating Characteristic) — construction, AUC (Area Under Curve), comparison of tests
Cut-off values — trade-off between sensitivity and specificity, clinical decision thresholds
Screening vs diagnostic tests — characteristics, requirements for screening tests (Wilson & Jungner criteria)
Gold standard — definition, verification bias, imperfect gold standard
Agreement and reliability — Cohen's kappa, interpretation (poor to perfect agreement), intra-observer and inter-observer variability
Classification of study designs — observational vs interventional, descriptive vs analytical
Case report and case series — definition, uses, limitations
Cross-sectional study (prevalence study) — design, advantages, limitations, measures (prevalence, OR)
Ecological study — unit of analysis is population, ecological fallacy
Case-control study — design, selection of cases and controls, matching, odds ratio, advantages, limitations
Nested case-control study — within a cohort, advantages
Cohort study — prospective vs retrospective, design, relative risk, attributable risk, advantages, limitations
Historical cohort study — using existing records
Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) — design, phases (I–IV), CONSORT statement
Randomization — simple, block, stratified, cluster, adaptive, allocation concealment
Blinding — single, double, triple blind, open-label, sham procedures
Placebo and placebo effect — ethical use, active comparator
Intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis vs per-protocol analysis — advantages, limitations
Crossover study design — washout period, carryover effect
Factorial design — testing multiple interventions simultaneously
Quasi-experimental studies — non-randomized, before-after studies, interrupted time series
Qualitative research — methods (interviews, focus groups, ethnography), thematic analysis, grounded theory
Mixed methods research — combining quantitative and qualitative approaches
Phases of clinical trials — Phase I (safety), Phase II (efficacy), Phase III (comparative), Phase IV (post-marketing surveillance)
Adaptive trial designs — interim analysis, sample size re-estimation

topics.topic: Bias, Confounding & Error in Research (~15 questions)
subtopics: Bias — definition, classification (selection bias, information bias, confounding)
Selection bias — types (Berkson's bias, Neyman bias, volunteer bias, healthy worker effect, loss to follow-up)
Information bias — recall bias, interviewer bias, observer bias, reporting bias, Hawthorne effect
Measurement bias — misclassification (differential, non-differential), instrument error
Lead-time bias — in screening studies, apparent vs real survival benefit
Length-time bias — screening detects slower-growing diseases
Publication bias — positive result bias, funnel plot, file drawer problem
Attrition bias — differential loss to follow-up
Confounding — definition, identification, control methods
Methods to control confounding — randomization, restriction, matching, stratification, multivariable analysis, propensity score
Effect modification (interaction) — difference from confounding, assessment, reporting
Internal validity vs external validity (generalizability)
Reliability — test-retest, inter-rater, intra-rater, Cronbach's alpha
Validity — content, criterion (concurrent, predictive), construct validity
Precision vs accuracy — random error vs systematic error
Evidence-based medicine — definition (Sackett), three pillars (best evidence, clinical expertise, patient values)
Hierarchy of evidence — pyramid (expert opinion → case series → case-control → cohort → RCT → systematic review/meta-analysis)
Levels of evidence and grades of recommendation — Oxford CEBM, GRADE system
Asking clinical questions — PICO framework (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome)
Searching for evidence — PubMed, Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, search strategies, MeSH terms
Critical appraisal of literature — validity, results, applicability, CASP checklists
Systematic review — definition, steps (protocol, search, selection, data extraction, quality assessment, synthesis)
PRISMA statement — reporting guidelines for systematic reviews
Meta-analysis — definition, forest plot (point estimates, CI, diamond), heterogeneity (I², Q statistic, Cochran's Q)
Fixed-effect vs random-effects model — when to use each
Heterogeneity — clinical, methodological, statistical, sources, management (subgroup analysis, meta-regression)
Funnel plot — detection of publication bias, Egger's test
Sensitivity analysis — assessing robustness of meta-analysis results
Clinical practice guidelines — development, AGREE II instrument, adaptation
Knowledge translation — implementation of evidence into practice, barriers, facilitators

topics.topic: Medical Jurisprudence Overlap — Negligence & Malpractice (~15 questions)
subtopics: Medical negligence — definition, elements (duty of care, breach of duty, causation, damage)
Standard of care — Bolam test (Bolam vs Friern Hospital), Bolitho modification
Res ipsa loquitur — "the thing speaks for itself," application in medical negligence
Contributory negligence — patient's role in adverse outcome
Vicarious liability — employer's liability for employee's negligence, hospital liability
Civil vs criminal negligence — burden of proof, consequences
Criminal negligence in India — Section 304A IPC (causing death by negligence), Jacob Mathew vs State of Punjab (2005) — Supreme Court guidelines
Consumer Protection Act 2019 — medical negligence as deficiency in service, compensation, District/State/National Commission
Landmark cases in medical negligence — Indian Medical Association vs V.P. Shantha, Samira Kohli vs Dr. Prabha Manchanda, Malay Kumar Ganguly vs Dr. Sukumar Mukherjee
Professional indemnity insurance — importance, coverage
Defensive medicine — definition, positive and negative defensive medicine, impact on healthcare
Medical audit and clinical governance — quality improvement, peer review
Adverse events and medical errors — classification, root cause analysis, Swiss cheese model
Patient safety — WHO initiatives, reporting systems, just culture
Grievance redressal mechanisms — hospital committees, medical councils, consumer forums, courts
Medical records — definition, types, importance (clinical, legal, research, administrative)
Components of medical records — history, examination, investigations, diagnosis, treatment, consent, discharge summary
Legal status of medical records — admissibility as evidence, Indian Evidence Act
Retention of medical records — duration, guidelines, digital records
Electronic Health Records (EHR) — advantages, challenges, interoperability, data security
Medico-legal case (MLC) — definition, when to register, documentation, police intimation
Death certificate — format, cause of death certification (ICD coding), who can issue
Wound certificate and injury report — documentation, legal importance
Prescription writing — legal requirements, legibility, abbreviations, e-prescriptions
Discharge summary — components, medicolegal importance, patient's right to records
Legal framework of consent in India — Indian Contract Act, IPC sections (Section 87, 88, 89, 90, 92)
Age of consent for medical treatment — Indian Majority Act 1875 (18 years), exceptions
Consent in emergency — Section 92 IPC, Good Samaritan Law (Supreme Court guidelines 2016, Motor Vehicles Amendment Act 2019)
Consent for mentally ill — Mental Healthcare Act 2017, advance directives, nominated representative
Consent for HIV testing — NACO guidelines, preand post-test counseling
Patient rights — Charter of Patient Rights (NHRC), right to information, right to choose, right to privacy, right to grievance redressal
Right to access medical records — patient's right, hospital's obligation
Refusal of treatment — competent adult's right, documentation, against medical advice (AMA) discharge
Consent in clinical research — ICMR guidelines, additional safeguards for vulnerable populations
Informed refusal — documentation, medicolegal protection
